reason: The text passage (1 Samuel 28-30) contains abundant examples of Hebrew people (Israelites) freely expressing their views, feelings, and concerns. David speaks openly to Achish about his intentions; the woman at En-dor boldly questions Saul about his deception (וַתֹּאמֶר הָאִשָּׁה אֶל־ שָׁאוּל לָמָּה רִמִּיתָנִי - 'Why have you deceived me?'); Samuel speaks directly to Saul; David consults with his priest Abiathar; David inquires of God; and David's men openly weep and express their anguish about their families. The narrative demonstrates free dialogue, consultation, questioning authority, and emotional expression without any indication of discouragement from speaking.
